Active predictions are updated throughout market hours. Once a prediction concludes, it moves to the Closed Predictions archive with the simulated profit or loss percentage. Subscribers can view active signals in real time on the dashboard or fetch them programmatically via the [REST API](https://sharepredictions.com/api/docs/api-documentation/), while the full closed history and cumulative profit chart are available to everyone.

The P/L percentage reflects the premium price change based on the prediction outcome:

*   **Stop Loss only** — 100% of the position was closed at the stop-loss level
*   **1st Target + Stop Loss** — half sold at the 1st target profit, the other half hit stop loss; P/L is the average
*   **1st Target only** — half sold at the 1st target, remaining half expired; P/L is half the 1st target gain
*   **2nd Target** — half sold at the 1st target, half at the 2nd target; P/L is the average of both
*   **Expired** — position expired without hitting any target or stop loss

Hover over any P/L value in the closed predictions table to see the exact calculation for that specific prediction.

Mobile app subscriptions are separate from the web/API subscription. The web subscription includes both the Predictions Dashboard (Web) and the API. App subscriptions don't grant API access, and API subscriptions don't unlock in‑app premium features.

Subscriptions renew automatically and can be canceled anytime. We don't provide pro‑rata refunds for unused time or credits; you'll retain access until the end of the current billing period.

You can cancel your subscription at any time by clicking the "Manage Subscription" button on your profile page.

Our predictions are algorithmic, short‑term probability estimates and are provided for informational purposes only. They are not financial advice and there's no guarantee of accuracy. Use them alongside your own research and technical/fundamental analysis.

acceptedAnswer.text: A bullish signal is an indicator suggesting a potential upward price movement in a security or market.
A bearish signal is an indicator suggesting a potential downward price movement in a security or market.
A market barometer is an overall assessment of market conditions and sentiment that helps traders understand the general direction of the market.

mainEntity.name: What are the Magnificent Seven stocks?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Magnificent Seven are the most influential technology companies: Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet/Google (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), NVIDIA (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA), and Meta Platforms (META). These stocks often drive broader market sentiment and trends.

mainEntity.name: How do the AI Options Predictions work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our AI scans the options market daily and publishes call and put predictions with a buy target, two sell targets for profit-taking, and a stop-loss level. Active predictions update throughout market hours. Once concluded, each prediction moves to the closed archive showing the simulated profit or loss percentage. Subscribers can also access active and concluded options signals programmatically via the REST API.

mainEntity.name: How is the P/L percentage calculated for options predictions?

acceptedAnswer.text: P/L is based on the premium price change at the outcome level. If only the stop loss is hit, 100% of the position is closed there. If the 1st target and stop loss are both hit, P/L is the average of each half. If both targets are hit, P/L averages the 1st and 2nd target gains. Hover over any P/L value in the closed predictions table to see the exact breakdown.
